summary: The root ذبذب (dhbdhb) primarily describes a state of wavering, oscillation, or being in suspense between two things.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
parts_note: parts[].k: d=Lane's English rendering, a=Arabic, p=apparatus/citation

entries.text: الذَّبْذَبُ : اللّسانُ؛ خيرٌ للإنسان أن يضبط ذبذبَه ولا يتركه طليقاً مطلقاً.

classical_note: Arabic-only entries from public-domain classical lexica, ordered by compiler death date. Tier 'root-semantic' (Maqayis) derives all senses of a root from one core idea. Tier 'interpretive' (Mufradat) cites hadith and takes theological positions and is not equivalent evidence. Compilation: wizsk/arabic_lexicons, GPL-3.0.
